Figure 1: Trial profile. CONSORT diagram showing enrolment, allocation, and analysis populations at interim and final stages. First stage: 107 assessed for eligibility; 59 excluded (35 did not meet inclusion criteria; 24 declined); 48 enrolled and randomly assigned. Placebo: 12 allocated; 1 did not receive allocated intervention (drop-out), 1 lost to follow-up; 11 completed treatment, 12 included in ITT interim analysis; second-stage placebo: 11 allocated, 1 did not receive allocated intervention (drop-out), 1 missed scheduled visits; 10 completed treatment, 11 included in ITT analysis; total 23 included in final ITT analysis. CBD 200 mg: 12 allocated; 2 did not receive allocated intervention (drop-out; 1 missed scheduled visits, 1 poor medication adherence); 10 completed treatment, 12 included in ITT interim analysis; ineffective dose eliminated from trial. CBD 400 mg: 12 allocated; 1 did not receive allocated intervention (drop-out), 1 use of psychotropic medication during treatment; 11 completed treatment, 12 included in ITT interim analysis; second stage: 12 allocated, all received allocated intervention, 12 completed treatment and included in ITT analysis; total 24 included in final ITT analysis. CBD 800 mg: 12 allocated, all received allocated intervention, 12 completed treatment and included in ITT interim analysis; second stage 11 allocated, all received allocated intervention, 11 completed treatment and included in ITT analysis; total 23 included in final ITT analysis. Second stage: 80 assessed for eligibility; 46 excluded (28 did not meet inclusion criteria; 18 declined); 34 enrolled and randomly assigned.

bases.stopping_rationale: Inspected the main report's participant-flow figure, Results and missing-data methods, plus the supplement's statistical methods and final endpoint table. The table provides estimates, not observed/imputed participant counts; searches for missing outcomes, follow-up loss and sensitivity analysis did not locate such counts. The original registry bytes are unavailable, so no source-grounded protocol/registry detail can resolve this remaining count and ascertainment uncertainty.
bases.unresolved_premise: The exact randomized-participant outcome-observed and imputed counts for this arm-specific weeks 1–4 urine outcome are not reported, and treatment completion does not establish urinary measurement at each scheduled visit.

counterevidence.implication: Although 94% completed treatment with all treatment-week visits, the trial reports missing outcomes requiring imputation, so completion and ITT membership cannot establish complete outcome ascertainment.

answers.justification: For the approved weeks 1–4 urinary THC-COOH:creatinine outcome, the report says 77/82 randomized participants (94%) completed treatment, defined in part by attending all treatment-week visits, while the final ITT analysis included all 23 placebo and 24 CBD 400 mg participants. This supports, but does not prove, that data were available for nearly all participants. The authors also report that some missing outcomes were multiply imputed; completion and analysis denominators are not outcome-observation counts. Given the high reported treatment-visit completion and no evidence of extensive outcome loss, probably yes is reasonable, but exact arm-specific observed/imputed counts and the impact of missing values remain unknown.
